# dsh-lead-mode
English | 中文
Adds a Lead mode to DSH. One preset, two skills, one self-check command, two reminders.
The official Team runtime ships tools: `spawn_teammate`, `send_message`, `team_task_*`. When to dele
gate, whom to delegate to, how to wait for a result, how to write the closing message, how to merge
several members' output: none of that is in the tools. This plugin adds that layer. It does not repl
ace the official Team mode; it sits on top of it.
Once installed, the model works the way a Lead does: split the work, delegate it, accept the result.
It delegates hands-on work instead of doing everything alone.
## What you get
Five things. None of them touch dsh itself.
| Capability | Entry point | What you do |

| Lead mode preset | "Lead 模式" in the preset list | Switch to it |
| Lead working method skill | `/s

kill lead-mode`; the model also loads it on its own | Nothing |
| Team digest skill | `/skill team-d

igest`; the model decides at wrap-up whether to write one | Nothing |
| Dependency self-check | `/le

ad-mode` | Run it when dependencies look wrong |
| Two upfront reminders | Automatic | Nothing |
Additive only. `cordis.patch.yml` holds exactly two `insert` rows: this plugin, and a new `lead-mode
` preset. The official `standard` preset is untouched; the new one copies 21 of its rows field for f
ield and swaps only the persona.
It registers no tools, listens to no agent lifecycle events, and intercepts no requests. `lib/index.
js` writes to two registries only: `skills` (two entries) and `commands` (one), plus a single warn a
t startup. Uninstall the plugin and those entries are gone; official behaviour goes back to what it
artup. Uninstall the plugin and those entries are gone; official behaviour goes back to what it was.
The one place it can collide is a skill or command with the same name. If you already have `lead-mod
e` or `team-digest`, the host takes the first one it sees, warns, and ignores ours; a collision mean

### 1. The Lead mode preset
Switch to it and the session's model becomes a Lead.
The preset is the official `standard` preset row for row, all 22 of them, with only the persona repl
aced. No tool is dropped: bash, file read/write, search, web, todo, skill, goal, plan, compaction, s
ubagent and workflow are all there.
So switching to Lead mode costs you no capability. It changes how the model works, not what it can d
switching to Lead mode costs you no capability. It changes how the model works, not what it can do.
### 2. The Lead working method skill
A working method for splitting, delegating and accepting work, shipped inside the package.
It is not tied to the preset. Any session can load it, two ways:

- The model loads it when it judges the task needs it (the skill is marked model-invocable)
- You ru
n `/skill lead-mode` yourself
[该节后续省略]
### 3. The team digest skill
At wrap-up the team's output sits in N closing messages and N worklogs, with nothing merging them. T
his skill writes it into one `reports/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<effort>.md`.
[该节后续省略]
### Why point there at all
Tool calls read one at a time. `list_agents` gives one line of status; `team_task_list` gives task o
wnership. Seeing who is doing what, and who said what to whom, takes a page.
dsh-context adds a **Fleet / 编队** tab to every session (right of **Context**), and the right sidebar
's **Context** panel carries the same card.
| Surface | Shows |

| Summary | Member status, live context, estimated cost, task progress |
| Agent Network | The curre

nt agent, its parents, every subagent, one card each |
| Fleet Members | Each member's role, model,

latest reply, run time, steps, active task count |
| Tasks | Team tasks and subagent delegations tog

ether, grouped by owner, with blocked-by chains |
| Agent Comms | Who said what to whom. Team relays
, mailbox deliveries, and the runtime's settlement notices |
Picking a member on the graph or the member board narrows Tasks and Agent Comms to that one agent. O
pening a message in Agent Comms shows the full record: which session log it came from, its sequence,
whether the runtime wrote the settlement notice or the child sent it, and the complete closing repo

## Why the install command pins a version
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team-profile` has three dist-tags on npm:
| dist-tag | Version | Host it fits |

| `latest` | 0.1.5-alpha.2 | 0.1.x |
| `alpha` | 0.2.2-alpha.3 | an earlier preview of the 0.2.2 lin
Bare package name resolves `latest`, which installs 0.1.5-alpha.2. That build targets 0.1.x hosts an
d does not mount on a 0.2.2 host. After installing it, no Team tools appear in dsh and `/lead-mode`
still reports "not mounted".
Measured on 2026-10-26 with npm 11.20.0:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
So every install command in this plugin carries `@0.2.2-rc.1`: the persona prefix, the `/lead-mode`
output, the startup warn, and SKILL.md. `test/preset.test.mjs` and `test/smoke.test.mjs` both assert
that string, so a future edit cannot quietly drop back to the bare name.
`next` now points at `0.2.2-rc.1`, the build this plugin pins; `alpha` (`0.2.2-alpha.3`) is an earli
er preview of the same line.
## Why the preset does not carry the Team runtime
`apply()` in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-tool-agent-team` listens on the global `agent/created` e
vent and installs Team tools on every agent. It is a host-plane plugin; putting it in a preset would
leak it into every session.
So this plugin stays at: preset, two skills, reminder. Whether the Team runtime is on is decided by
the user through the official profile package.
